package_info.package_versions: versions vulnerable to CVE-2021-30116 (exact versions not specified in report)
package_info.why_malicious: Kaseya VSA (on-premises) was exploited via a zero-day vulnerability (CVE-2021-30116) that allowed unauthenticated remote attackers to execute arbitrary commands on the VSA server. Attackers leveraged this to distribute ransomware to managed endpoints at scale, causing widespread business disruption and extortion.

execution_context.file_location: Kaseya VSA web interface (vulnerable endpoint exposed to internet)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Attackers exploited a pre-authentication remote code execution (RCE) vulnerability (CVE-2021-30116) by sending specially crafted HTTP requests to the Kaseya VSA server, bypassing authentication controls and executing arbitrary system commands on the server and, through it, on managed endpoints.
malicious_snippets.code_language: unknown (exploit payload delivered via HTTP, likely shell or PowerShell commands)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code is triggered by a remote, unauthenticated HTTP request exploiting the RCE vulnerability, which results in arbitrary system command execution on the Kaseya VSA server; these commands are then used to stage and propagate malicious payloads to managed endpoints, enabling further compromise.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Pre-authentication RCE enabling arbitrary command execution on a remote management server is a critical security risk, as it allows attackers to bypass all authentication and authorization mechanisms and gain full control over the system.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal operation requires strict authentication and authorization before any command execution; this exploit bypasses all access controls, violating the core security model of remote management software.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate remote management tools may execute commands on endpoints, but only after successful authentication and authorization by an administrator.
key_indicators: Pre-authentication access to command execution endpoints
Arbitrary system command execution via unauthenticated HTTP requests
Abuse of management server to stage and distribute malicious payloads

execution_context.file_location: Managed endpoint (deployed via Kaseya VSA agent)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Ransomware payload delivered to endpoints via Kaseya VSA agent, which encrypts files on the system and displays a ransom note to the user.
malicious_snippets.code_language: unknown (ransomware binary, likely Windows PE executable)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: After post-exploitation deployment, the code executes on managed endpoints, encrypts user and system files, and creates ransom note files on the desktop and in affected directories, resulting in data inaccessibility and extortion demands.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Deployment of ransomware through IT management software is highly anomalous and malicious, as it weaponizes trusted infrastructure to maximize impact.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Endpoint management agents are expected to deliver legitimate software updates or scripts, never ransomware or destructive payloads.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Endpoint management tools may deploy software or scripts for maintenance, but never code that encrypts files or demands ransom.
key_indicators: Mass deployment of ransomware binaries to endpoints via management agent
File encryption activity initiated by remote management software
Creation of ransom note files (e.g., README.txt, ransom.txt) on endpoints

attack_chain.action: Attacker exploits pre-authentication RCE vulnerability (CVE-2021-30116) in Kaseya VSA server by sending crafted HTTP requests, gaining arbitrary code execution on the server.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker obtains the ability to execute arbitrary commands on the VSA server and, by extension, on all managed endpoints.

attack_chain.action: Attacker leverages VSA server's management functionality to deploy ransomware payloads to all managed endpoints using the agent update mechanism.
attack_chain.leads_to: Ransomware executes on endpoints, encrypts files, and displays ransom notes, resulting in widespread business disruption and extortion.

behavioral_signatures: Unusual command execution on Kaseya VSA server without prior authentication
Mass deployment of new or unexpected executable files to endpoints via the VSA agent
Simultaneous file encryption and ransom note creation across multiple managed endpoints
file_indicators: Unexpected executable files delivered to endpoints via Kaseya VSA agent (e.g., unknown .exe or .dll files in agent update directories)
Ransom note files such as README.txt or ransom.txt appearing on user desktops and in affected directories
network_indicators: Unusual outbound connections from Kaseya VSA server or endpoints to external, attacker-controlled infrastructure
Spike in network traffic from VSA server to all managed endpoints, especially involving executable file transfers
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor Kaseya VSA server logs for pre-authentication access and command execution attempts on management endpoints. Alert on mass deployment of new executables or scripts to managed endpoints, especially if followed by file encryption or ransom note creation. Detect the appearance of ransom note files and monitor for unusual outbound network connections from VSA servers or endpoints to unrecognized external addresses.
